title: Generating interesting scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs: Evaluations with 100 research group leaders
summary_zh: 本文研究利用知识图谱和LLM生成科学想法。方法上，构建了包含5800万篇论文的知识图谱，并使用LLM生成个性化想法。实验表明，专家对生成的想法兴趣评分适中。
summary_en: This paper studies generating scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs. The method constructs a knowledge graph of 58 million papers and uses an LLM to generate personalized ideas. Experiments show that experts rate the generated ideas moderately interesting.
insights: 创新点：利用知识图谱和LLM生成个性化科学想法
方法亮点：构建了大规模知识图谱，并使用LLM进行个性化生成
关键发现：专家对生成的想法兴趣评分适中
insights_en: Novelty: Generating personalized scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs
Method highlight: Constructing a large-scale knowledge graph and using LLM for personalized generation
Key finding: Experts rate the generated ideas moderately interesting
abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature makes it increasingly challenging for researchers to identify novel and impactful ideas, especially across disciplines. Modern AI systems offer new opportunities for scientific ideation, but how compelling are AI-generated ideas, and how can their quality be improved? Here, we introduce SCIMUSE , which generates personalized research ideas using a knowledge graph of 58 million papers and a large language model (LLM). A central focus of this work is to understand how interesting these ideas are. Therefore, we conducted a large-scale evaluation in which more than 100 research group leaders—spanning the natural sciences to the humanities—rated over 4,400 personalized ideas according to their level of interest. Overall, expert ratings were modest (mean 2.40 on a 5-point scale, most common rating 1), while 24.9% of ideas were rated 4 or 5. We find that supplying concept pairs selected using the knowledge graph does not improve expert-rated interest over a titles-only GPT baseline. High-citation-predicted pairs even showed a weak tendency (1.94 σ ) toward lower interest than random pairs. Nevertheless, graph features can be used to control properties of ideas, and, using this unique evaluation dataset, we show that idea interest can be predicted with both a supervised neural network based on graph features and a zero-shot ranking approach based on an LLM. Our work provides an AI methodology for generating scientific ideas and a large-scale interdisciplinary expert evaluation, paving the way to study and improve difficult-to-measure metrics such as expert-perceived scientific interestingness.

title: Mitigating Covariate Shift in Behavioral Cloning via Robust Stationary Distribution Correction
summary_zh: 本文研究行为克隆中的协变量偏移问题。提出基于稳健的平稳分布校正方法。实验表明，该方法有效减轻了偏移。
summary_en: This paper investigates the covariate shift issue in behavioral cloning. A robust stationary distribution correction method is proposed. Experiments show that this method effectively mitigates the shift.
insights: 创新点：提出稳健的平稳分布校正方法
方法亮点：有效减轻协变量偏移
关键发现：方法在行为克隆中有效
insights_en: Novelty: Proposed a robust stationary distribution correction method
Method highlight: Effectively mitigates covariate shift
Key finding: Method is effective in behavioral cloning
abstract: We consider offline imitation learning (IL), which aims to train an agent to imitate from the dataset of expert demonstrations without online interaction with the environment. Behavioral Cloning (BC) has been a simple yet effective approach to offline IL, but it is also well-known to be vulnerable to the covariate shift resulting from the mismatch between the state distributions induced by the learned policy and the expert policy. Moreover, as often occurs in practice, when expert datasets are collected from an arbitrary state distribution instead of a stationary one, these shifts become more pronounced, potentially leading to substantial failures in existing IL methods. Specifically, we focus on covariate shift resulting from arbitrary state data distributions, such as biased data collection or incomplete trajectories, rather than shifts induced by changes in dynamics or noisy expert actions. In this paper, to mitigate the effect of the covariate shifts in BC, we propose DrilDICE, which utilizes a distributionally robust BC objective by employing a stationary distribution correction ratio estimation (DICE) to derive a feasible solution. We evaluate the effectiveness of our method through an extensive set of experiments covering diverse covariate shift scenarios. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach in improving the robustness against the shifts, outperforming existing offline IL methods in such scenarios.

title: Intrinsically motivated humans and agents in open-world exploration
summary_zh: 研究比较人类、儿童和AI在开放世界探索中的内在动机。方法上，使用Crafter环境研究熵、信息增益和赋权。实验表明，三者与探索进度正相关，熵和赋权在儿童中更相关。
summary_en: This study compares intrinsic motivation in humans, children, and AI agents in open-world exploration. The method involves using the Crafter environment to study entropy, information gain, and empowerment. Experiments show that all three are positively correlated with exploration progress, with entropy and empowerment more strongly related to children's progress.
insights: 创新点：比较人类、儿童和AI的内在动机
方法亮点：使用Crafter环境研究探索动机
关键发现：熵和赋权与儿童探索进度更相关
insights_en: Novelty: Comparing intrinsic motivation in humans, children, and AI agents
Method highlight: Studying exploration motivation using the Crafter environment
Key finding: Entropy and empowerment are more strongly related to children's exploration progress
abstract: What drives exploration? Understanding the intrinsic motivation to explore is a long-standing challenge in both cognitive science and AI. In this study, we directly compare adults, children aged 8 to 12 y, and AI agents exploring a complex, open-ended environment called Crafter ( 1 ). We study how three common information-theoretic intrinsic objectives—entropy, information gain, and empowerment—relate to their behavior. We find that all three are positively correlated with human exploration progress for both children and adults, although entropy and empowerment are more strongly related to exploration progress in children than information gain. Furthermore, across agents and humans we observe that entropy initially increases rapidly, then plateaus, while empowerment increases continuously, suggesting that in early exploration they look for novel states, while in advanced exploration they look for states they can control. Finally, we find preliminary evidence that private speech about goals may aid exploration in children. Our data are available at https://github.com/alyd/humans_in_crafter_data .

title: Person Recognition at Altitude and Range: Fusion of Face, Body Shape and Gait
summary_zh: 本文研究高空远距离人体识别问题。提出FarSight系统，融合面部、步态和体型特征。实验表明系统有效识别人体。
summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of person recognition at altitude and range. The proposed FarSight system fuses face, gait, and body shape features. Experiments show the system effectively recognizes individuals.
insights: 创新点：融合多模态生物特征进行识别
方法亮点：提出统一的端到端识别系统
关键发现：系统在复杂环境下表现良好
insights_en: Novelty: Fusion of multimodal biometric features for recognition
Method highlight: A unified end-to-end recognition system proposed
Key finding: The system performs well in complex environments
abstract: We address the problem of whole-body person recognition in unconstrained environments. This problem arises in surveillance scenarios such as those in the IARPA Biometric Recognition and Identification at Altitude and Range (BRIAR) program, where biometric data is captured at long standoff distances, elevated viewing angles, and under adverse atmospheric conditions (e.g., turbulence and high wind velocity). To this end, we propose FarSight, a unified end-to-end system for person recognition that integrates complementary biometric cues across face, gait, and body shape modalities. FarSight comprises four core modules: multi-subject detection and tracking, recognition-aware video restoration, modality-specific biometric feature encoding, and quality-guided multi-modal fusion. Rather than treating these modules as independent processing stages, FarSight coordinates key stage-level decisions around the final biometric objective: tracking maintains identity-consistent temporal evidence, restoration is selectively invoked and optimized for recognition, and modality-quality estimates guide score fusion. This coordinated design supports recognition under degraded image conditions, large pose and scale variations, and cross-domain gaps. Extensive experiments on the BRIAR dataset, one of the most comprehensive benchmarks for long-range, multi-modal biometric recognition, demonstrate the effectiveness of FarSight. Compared with our preliminary system [1] on the Face-Included treatment set of BRIAR EVP 5.0.1, the current system improves 1:1 verification (TAR@0.1% FAR) by 34.4 percentage points and closed-set identification (Rank-20) by 17.8 percentage points, while reducing open-set identification errors (FNIR@1% FPIR) by 34.3 percentage points. Furthermore, FarSight was evaluated in the 2025 NIST RTE Face in Video Evaluation (FIVE), which conducts standardized face recognition testing on the BRIAR dataset. These results establish FarSight as a state-of-the-art solution for operational biometric recognition in challenging real-world conditions.

The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
summary_zh: 本文研究认知控制下认知地图的表征几何。通过功能磁共振成像和神经网络模型分析，发现任务相关和无关维度。
summary_en: This paper investigates the representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control. Functional MRI and neural network model analyses reveal task-related and irrelevant dimensions.
insights: 创新点：认知控制影响认知地图的表征几何
方法亮点：结合功能磁共振成像和神经网络模型
关键发现：发现任务相关和无关维度
insights_en: Novelty: Cognitive control affects the representational geometry of cognitive maps
Method highlight: Combining functional MRI and neural network models
Key finding: Dimensions related and irrelevant to the task are identified
abstract: Abstract Recent work has shown that the brain abstracts non-spatial relationships between entities or task states into representations called cognitive maps. Here, we investigate how cognitive control enables flexible top-down selection of goal-relevant information from multidimensional cognitive maps retrieved from memory. We examine the relationship between cognitive control and representational geometry by conducting parallel analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data and recurrent neural network models trained to perform the same task. We find both stable map-like representations in a medial temporal lobe and orbitofrontal cortical network that reflect both task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions and context-dependent, orthogonal representations of only task-relevant dimensions in a frontoparietal network. These representational motifs also emerge with distinct temporal profiles over the course of training in the recurrent neural network, with map-like representations appearing first. We further show that increasing control demands due to incongruence (conflicting responses) between current task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions impact the geometry of subjective representations, and the degree of this effect further accounts for individual differences in cognitive control. Taken together, our findings show how complementary representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, and reveal an intricate relationship between cognitive control and cognitive map geometry.

title: AnyNav: Visual neuro-symbolic friction learning for off-road navigation
summary_zh: 研究越野导航问题。提出基于神经符号的视觉摩擦估计和导航框架。结合视觉感知和物理模型。
summary_en: Studies off-road navigation. Introduces a vision-based friction estimation and navigation framework grounded in neuro-symbolic principles. Integrates visual perception with a physical model.
insights: 创新点：结合视觉感知和物理模型
方法亮点：神经符号方法应用于导航
关键发现：提高导航在复杂环境中的泛化能力
insights_en: Novelty: Integrates visual perception with a physical model
Method highlight: Applies neuro-symbolic methods to navigation
Key finding: Improves navigation generalization in complex environments
abstract: Off-road navigation is critical for a wide range of field robotics applications from planetary exploration to disaster response. However, it remains a longstanding challenge due to unstructured environments and the inherently complex terrain–vehicle interactions. Traditional physics-based methods struggle to accurately capture the nonlinear dynamics underlying these interactions, while purely data-driven approaches often overfit to specific motion patterns, vehicle geometries, or platforms, limiting their generalization in diverse, real-world scenarios. To address these limitations, we introduce AnyNav, a vision-based friction estimation and navigation framework grounded in neuro-symbolic principles. Our approach integrates neural networks for visual perception with symbolic physical models for reasoning about terrain-vehicle dynamics. To enable learning in a self-supervised manner for real-world settings, we adopt the imperative learning paradigm, where a bilevel optimization framework leverages physics-based optimization for training the friction network. This explicit incorporation of physical reasoning substantially improves generalization across terrains, vehicle types, and operating conditions. Leveraging the predicted friction coefficients, we further develop a physics-informed navigation system capable of generating physically feasible, time-efficient paths together with corresponding speed profiles. We demonstrate that AnyNav seamlessly transfers from simulation to real-world robotic platforms, exhibiting strong robustness across different four-wheeled vehicles and diverse off-road environments.

title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
Recent advances in multi-agent human trajectory prediction: A comprehensive review
summary_zh: 综述了基于深度学习的多智能体轨迹预测的最新进展。分类现有方法，并强调多智能体轨迹预测的关键挑战和未来研究方向。
summary_en: Reviews the latest advancements in deep learning-based multi-agent trajectory prediction. Categorizes existing methods and highlights key challenges and future research directions in multi-agent trajectory prediction.
insights: 创新点：综述了多智能体轨迹预测的最新进展
方法亮点：分类现有方法
关键发现：强调未来研究方向
insights_en: Novelty: Reviews the latest advancements in multi-agent trajectory prediction
Method highlight: Categorizes existing methods
Key finding: Emphasizes future research directions
abstract: With the emergence of powerful data-driven methods in human trajectory prediction (HTP), gaining a finer understanding of multi-agent interactions lies within hand’s reach, with important implications in areas such as social robot navigation, autonomous driving, and crowd modeling. This survey reviews some of the most recent advancements in deep learning-based multi-agent trajectory prediction, focusing on studies published between 2020 and 2025. We categorize the existing methods based on their architectural design, their input representations, and their overall prediction strategies. Furthermore, we highlight key challenges and future research directions in multi-agent HTP.

title: GenHOI: Generalizing Text-driven 4D Human-Object Interaction Synthesis for Unseen Objects
Toward triggered generation of indistinguishable single photons from MoTe2 quantum emitters
summary_zh: 本文研究MoTe2量子发射器触发单光子生成。通过应变和缺陷工程，实现近红外量子发射器，具有高单光子纯度。
summary_en: This paper investigates triggered single-photon generation from MoTe2 quantum emitters. Near-infrared quantum emitters with high single-photon purity are realized through strain and defect engineering.
insights: 创新点：实现近红外量子发射器
方法亮点：应变和缺陷工程技术
关键发现：高单光子纯度
insights_en: Novelty: Realization of near-infrared quantum emitters
Method highlight: Strain and defect engineering techniques
Key finding: High single-photon purity
abstract: Single-photon sources operating at telecom wavelengths are fundamental components for long-distance optical quantum communication and information processing. Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides offer a promising platform for such sources, but their development has been hindered by limited spectral range and poor single-photon indistinguishability. Here, we demonstrate a reproducible approach for generating near-infrared (1090–1200 nm) quantum emitters in bilayer MoTe2 using deterministic strain and defect engineering. These emitters exhibit strong linear polarization, sub-nanosecond lifetimes, high single-photon purity (triggered g(2)(0) as low as ~0.01 under p-shell excitation), and resolution-limited emission. Electrostatic biasing enables spectral tuning, suppresses photon bunching, and shortens radiative lifetimes. Most notably, two-photon interference measurements reveal a Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility of ~7.1%, and up to ~60% with post-selection under p-shell excitation, which represents state-of-the-art performance for quantum emitters in the transition-metal dichalcogenide platform. These results establish MoTe2 as a viable platform for tunable, low-noise, high-purity single-photon sources for quantum photonics. Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides are promising single-photon platforms but achieving photon indistinguishability remains challenging. Here, the authors realize reproducible near-infrared quantum emitters in bilayer MoTe2 with high purity, electrical tunability, and record indistinguishability.

title: Language model teams as distributed systems
summary_zh: 研究LLM团队作为分布式系统的设计原则。提出基于分布式系统的框架，预测任务结构和团队架构对性能的影响。
summary_en: The study investigates design principles for LLM teams as distributed systems. A framework based on distributed systems is proposed to predict the impact of task structure and team architecture on performance.
insights: 创新点：将LLM团队视为分布式系统
方法亮点：提出基于分布式系统的框架
关键发现：任务结构和团队架构影响性能
insights_en: Novelty: Viewing LLM teams as distributed systems
Method highlight: Proposing a framework based on distributed systems
Key finding: Task structure and team architecture impact performance
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are growing increasingly powerful. Yet, fundamental constraints on the reasoning, memory, and performance of individual models has sparked recent interest in scaling abilities using LLM teams. With growing deployment of LLM teams at scale, there is a need for principled guidelines for when teams help, how many agents to use, and how structure impacts performance. Rather than building these teams through trial-and-error, we propose using distributed systems as a formal foundation for designing and evaluating LLM teams. Under this formal framework, we derive predictions about how task structure and team architecture should shape performance. Empirical evidence supports these predictions: LLM team scaling follows classical distributed computing laws based on the structure of a task, and centralized and decentralized architectures exhibit the asymmetric vulnerabilities predicted by distributed systems theory. These results establish distributed computing as a generative framework that yields testable, quantitative predictions about LLM team behavior and informs the construction of more efficient and capable teams.

title: Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
summary_zh: 本文研究分子合成维度中的拓扑边缘态。利用超冷极性分子实现一维合成晶格，探测拓扑性质。
summary_en: This paper investigates topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension. A one-dimensional synthetic lattice is realized using ultracold polar molecules to probe topological properties.
insights: 创新点：分子合成维度中的拓扑边缘态研究
方法亮点：利用超冷极性分子实现合成晶格
关键发现：探测到拓扑边缘态
insights_en: Novelty: Research on topological edge states in molecular synthetic dimensions
Method highlight: Realization of synthetic lattices using ultracold polar molecules
Key finding: Topological edge states are probed
abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

title: Conveyor-mode electron shuttling through a T-junction in Si/SiGe
summary_zh: 本文介绍了一种通过T-junction在Si/SiGe中进行电子穿梭的方法。实验测量了电子穿梭的保真度。结果表明，穿梭保真度高达100%。
summary_en: This paper introduces a method for electron shuttling through a T-junction in Si/SiGe. The fidelity of electron shuttling is measured experimentally. The results show that the fidelity is as high as 100%.
insights: 创新点：T-junction实现电子穿梭
方法亮点：无需额外控制线
关键发现：穿梭保真度极高
insights_en: Novelty: T-junction enables electron shuttling
Method highlight: No extra control lines required
Key finding: Extremely high fidelity of shuttling
abstract: Abstract Conveyor-mode shuttling in gated Si/SiGe devices enables adiabatic transfer of single electrons, electron patterns and spin qubits confined in quantum dots across several microns with a scalable number of signal lines. To realize their full potential, linear shuttle lanes must connect into a two-dimensional grid with controllable routing. We introduce a T-junction device linking two independently driven shuttle lanes. Electron routing across the junction requires no extra control lines beyond the four channels per conveyor belt. We measure an inter-lane charge transfer fidelity of $$F={100.0000000}_{-9\times 1{0}^{-7}}^{+0}\,\%$$ F = 100.0000000 − 9 × 1 0 − 7 + 0 % at an instantaneous electron velocity of 270 mm s −1 . The filling of 54 quantum dots is controlled by simple atomic pulses, allowing us to swap electron patterns, laying the groundwork for a native spin-qubit SWAP gate. This T-junction establishes a path towards scalable, two-dimensional quantum computing architectures with flexible spin qubit routing for quantum error correction.

title: A sublattice polarimeter to probe the quantum geometry of synthetic photonic lattices
summary_zh: 本文提出一种子晶格偏振仪，用于探测合成光子晶格的量子几何。通过空间光调制器控制相位和衰减，提取晶体轨道的振幅和相位。
summary_en: This paper proposes a sublattice polarimeter for probing the quantum geometry of synthetic photonic lattices. By using a spatial light modulator to apply controlled phase shifts and attenuations, the amplitude and phase of crystal orbitals are extracted.
insights: 创新点：子晶格偏振仪探测量子几何
方法亮点：空间光调制器控制相位和衰减
关键发现：提取晶体轨道振幅和相位
insights_en: Novelty: Sublattice polarimeter for probing quantum geometry
Method highlight: Spatial light modulator for phase and attenuation control
Key finding: Extraction of crystal orbital amplitude and phase
abstract: Measuring the electronic structure of crystalline materials is key in advancing our understanding of their physical properties. While techniques such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy have provided unprecedented insights into electronic orbitals of natural crystals, an equivalent tool to characterize photonic lattices is still lacking. Here, we introduce a sublattice polarimeter that enables full reconstruction of the Bloch wavefunctions in bipartite photonic lattices. Using a spatial light modulator to apply controlled phase shifts and attenuations to each sublattice, we extract the amplitude and phase of the crystal orbitals across the Brillouin zone, including close to band degeneracies. This allows experimentally accessing the Bloch Hamiltonian, thereby determining the quantum geometric tensor and the band Chern numbers. Beyond bipartite lattices, the method can be generalized to address multiple internal degrees of freedom, opening routes to experimentally probe complex topological structures such as trigonal warping, Chern insulators and Euler curvature in multiband settings. The authors introduce a sublattice polarimeter to measure the Bloch wavefunctions in bipartite photonic lattices. Using their method, they experimentally access the quantum metric, Berry curvature and band Chern numbers.

Sound2Vision: Generating Diverse Visuals from Audio through Cross-Modal Latent Alignment
summary_zh: 提出从音频生成视觉图像的方法，解决视听模态信息差距问题，通过音频特征与视觉信息融合实现跨模态对齐。
summary_en: Proposes a method to generate visual images from audio, addressing the information gap between auditory and visual signals by aligning audio-visual modalities through feature fusion.
insights: 创新点：跨模态生成新方法
方法亮点：音频特征与视觉信息融合
关键发现：显著优于现有方法
insights_en: Novelty: Novel cross-modal generation approach
Method highlight: Fusion of audio features with visual information
Key finding: Significantly outperforms existing methods
abstract: How does audio describe the world around us? In this work, we propose a method for generating images of visual scenes from diverse in-the-wild sounds. This cross-modal generation task is challenging due to the significant information gap between auditory and visual signals. We address this challenge by designing a model that aligns audio-visual modalities by enriching audio features with visual information and translating them into the visual latent space. These features are then fed into the pre-trained image generator to produce images. To enhance image quality, we use sound source localization to select audio-visual pairs with strong cross-modal correlations. Our method achieves substantially better results on the VEGAS and VGGSound datasets compared to previous work and demonstrates control over the generation process through simple manipulations to the input waveform or latent space. Furthermore, we analyze the geometric properties of the learned embedding space and demonstrate that our learning approach effectively aligns audio-visual signals for cross-modal generation. Based on this analysis, we show that our method is agnostic to specific design choices, showing its generalizability by integrating various model architectures and different types of audio-visual data.

title: The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning
Experience modifies the synaptome architecture in the developing and adult mouse brain
summary_zh: 研究经验如何影响小鼠大脑突触组架构。通过环境富集和单眼剥夺实验，发现突触组大规模重构。不同经验改变特定突触类型，与蛋白质周转率和连接组结构一致。
summary_en: This study investigates how experience influences the synaptome architecture in the mouse brain. Environmental enrichment and monocular deprivation experiments reveal large-scale reconfiguration of synapse populations, with specific synaptic types modified by different experiences, aligned with protein turnover rates and connectome architecture.
insights: 创新点：经验影响突触组架构的时空分布
方法亮点：通过环境富集和单眼剥夺实验研究
关键发现：不同经验改变特定突触类型，与蛋白质周转率和连接组结构一致
insights_en: Novelty: Experience affects the spatiotemporal distribution of the synaptome architecture
Method highlight: Studied through environmental enrichment and monocular deprivation experiments
Key finding: Different experiences modify specific synaptic types aligned with protein turnover rates and connectome architecture
abstract: Synaptome architecture describes the spatiotemporal distribution of highly diverse excitatory synapses throughout the brain. Whether and how this architecture is impacted by experience and sensory input is unknown. We found that environmental enrichment and monocular visual deprivation drive large-scale reconfiguration of excitatory synapse populations in more than one hundred regions of the mouse brain. Different experiences modify distinct subsets of synapse types and subtypes, with patterns aligned with protein turnover rates and connectome architecture. Similarity in experience-dependent reconfiguration during development and adulthood indicates shared mechanisms of synaptome adaptation across the lifespan. Our findings support a population-selection model in which experiences drive adaptation by selectively modifying synapse types and subtypes distributed across the brain. Experience-driven reconfiguration of synaptome architecture shares features with the response to aging, sleep deprivation, brain injury and genetic mutations, supporting a unifying principle of brain adaptation.

title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
summary_zh: 提出全集成钙钛矿极化子电路，结合强光学非线性和光子平台的高速度与可扩展性。实现室温波导激光、可控光路由等功能。
summary_en: Proposes fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits, combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability of photonic platforms, achieving room-temperature waveguide lasing and controllable optical routing.
insights: 创新点：全集成钙钛矿极化子电路的设计
方法亮点：结合光学非线性和光子平台特性
关键发现：实现室温波导激光
insights_en: Novelty: Design of fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
Method highlight: Combining optical nonlinearities with photonic platform characteristics
Key finding: Achieving room-temperature waveguide lasing
abstract: Abstract Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing 1 . Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses 2 . Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms 3–5 . However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

title: GraphBEV++: Multi-Modal Feature Alignment for Autonomous Driving
Open-world panoptic segmentation
summary_zh: 提出一种通用方法Con2MAV，用于开放世界全景分割。实验表明其在开放世界分割中的强大能力。
summary_en: A general method, Con2MAV, for open-world panoptic segmentation is proposed. Experiments highlight its compelling capabilities in open-world segmentation.
insights: 创新点：提出开放世界全景分割的通用方法。
方法亮点：Con2MAV方法在开放世界分割中表现优异。
关键发现：该方法在多种数据集上均表现出色。
insights_en: Novelty: Proposing a general method for open-world panoptic segmentation.
Method highlight: Con2MAV performs excellently in open-world segmentation.
Key finding: The method shows compelling performance across various datasets.
abstract: Robots need to be able to understand their surroundings in order to operate safely and robustly, and to interact with the surrounding environment. Robots deployed in unconstrained real-world scenarios must additionally be able to deal with novel situations and objects that have never been seen before. In this article, we tackle the problem of open-world panoptic segmentation, that is, the task of discovering new semantic categories and new object instances at test time, while enforcing consistency among the categories that we incrementally discover. We present Con2MAV, a general method for open-world panoptic segmentation. Experiments across a wide range of datasets, from road scenes to underwater environments, highlight its compelling capabilities in open-world segmentation and its competitive performance on known classes. We will open-source the implementation of our approach upon acceptance. In addition, we propose PANIC ( P anoptic AN omalies I n C ontext), a benchmark for evaluating open-world segmentation tasks in autonomous driving scenarios. This dataset, recorded with a multi-modal sensor suite mounted on a car, and then manually annotated, provides high-quality, pixel-wise annotations of anomalous objects at both semantic and instance level. PANIC contains 800 images, more than 50 unknown classes, that is, classes that do not appear in the training set, and over 4000 object instances, providing a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating open-world segmentation methods in autonomous driving scenarios. We provide competitions for multiple open-world segmentation tasks on a hidden test set. Our dataset and competitions are available at https://www.ipb.uni-bonn.de/data/panic .

EfficientVPR: Toward Efficient Visual Place Recognition via Scene-Aware Prompt Tuning and Adaptive Feature Enhancement
summary_zh: 提出EfficientVPR框架，通过场景感知提示调整和自适应特征增强实现高效视觉地点识别。
summary_en: Proposes the EfficientVPR framework for efficient visual place recognition through scene-aware prompt tuning and adaptive feature enhancement.
insights: 创新点：场景感知提示调整提升效率
方法亮点：自适应特征增强增强判别性
关键发现：实现速度与准确率平衡
insights_en: Novelty: Scene-aware prompt tuning improves efficiency
Method highlight: Adaptive feature enhancement enhances discriminative regions
Key finding: Achieving a balance between speed and accuracy
abstract: Visual place recognition (VPR) faces critical challenges in handling extreme environmental variations while meeting the computational constraints of practical applications. Current methods predominantly address these challenges by either scaling up model capacity or employing computationally intensive reranking stages, creating a significant efficiency bottleneck. To overcome this limitation, we propose EfficientVPR, a lightweight one-stage framework that achieves speed-accuracy trade-offs through two key innovations: i) a scene-aware visual prompt tuning method which adapts pretrained features with less parameters while dynamically adjusting to sample-specific characteristics, and ii) an instance-dependent key local feature enhancement module that further reinforces discriminative regions. Comprehensive evaluations on Pitts250k, MSLS, Eynsham, AmsterTime and SVOX demonstrate that our method establishes a new SOTA for DINOv2-small models by outperforming all same-scale competitors, and delivers a $73\times$ speedup with 60\% lower-dimensional features while maintaining competitive (within 2.5% average R@1 gap) against the SOTA DINOv2-large-based two-stage method. Our code will be available at https://github.com/WiniTang/EfficientVPR.

Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
summary_zh: 本文提出一种软体机器人和计算模型，用于研究心房颤动中的左心耳血流动力学。该模型结合了软体机器人模拟器和有限元分析。
summary_en: This paper presents a soft robotic and computational model for studying left atrial hemodynamics in atrial fibrillation. The model combines a soft robotic simulator and finite element analysis.
insights: 创新点：软体机器人和计算模型研究心房颤动
方法亮点：结合软体机器人模拟器和有限元分析
关键发现：模型模拟左心耳血流动力学
insights_en: Novelty: Soft robotic and computational model for studying atrial fibrillation
Method highlight: Combination of soft robotic simulator and finite element analysis
Key finding: Model simulates left atrial hemodynamics
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses significant clinical challenges due to the complex and variable geometry of the left atrial appendage (LAA), whose structure complicates the development of personalized interventions like LAA occlusion (LAAO) for stroke prevention Current reliance on animal models and cadavers for the assessment of left atrium (LA) and LAA to study AF-related disease and interventions raises reproducibility concerns, necessitating the development of high fidelity, physiologically relevant tools. To address this, we present a multimodal framework combining a soft robotic benchtop simulator, a lumped parameter model (LPM), and finite element analysis (FEA) to replicate LA function in sinus rhythm, atrial flutter, and AF. The system integrates 3D-printed, patient-specific LA geometries with soft robotic actuators to reproduce realistic wall motion and hemodynamics. A compact, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-compatible flow loop, driven by a soft robotic left ventricle (LV), eliminates bulky and non-physiological pulsatile pumps, allowing precise flow measurements and LAAO device testing under clinically relevant conditions. Complementary LPM and FEA models provide mechanistic insights, quantifying systemic hemodynamic changes and LA wall stress during disease and interventions. The models effectively replicate the clinical markers of atrial dysfunction and arrhythmia disorders, and their physiological accuracy is demonstrated through validation against human imaging and porcine models. The soft robotic LV's ability to drive the mock flow loop is validated in a hybrid synthetic-biological configuration within a swine circulatory system, where the soft robotic ventricle replaces native ventricular contraction to sustain systemic circulation. This scalable and versatile framework integrates experimental and computational techniques to advance cardiovascular biomechanics, supporting device development, clinical research/training, and personalized AF treatment to improve patient outcomes.

title: Theoretical frameworks for credit assignment via behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity
summary_zh: 研究通过行为时间尺度突触可塑性进行信用分配的理论框架。提出gBTSP框架，应用于前馈和循环网络中的无监督和监督任务。
summary_en: This study proposes a theoretical framework, gBTSP, for credit assignment via behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity. The framework is applied to unsupervised and supervised tasks in feedforward and recurrent networks.
insights: 创新点：提出gBTSP框架
方法亮点：应用于前馈和循环网络
关键发现：无监督gBTSP学习前馈网络中的位置场图，循环网络中的吸引子记忆
insights_en: Novelty: Proposal of the gBTSP framework
Method highlight: Application to feedforward and recurrent networks
Key finding: Unsupervised gBTSP learns place field maps in feedforward networks and attractor memories in recurrent networks
abstract: Abstract Behavioral Timescale Synaptic Plasticity (BTSP) is a form of plasticity which drives place field formation in hippocampal pyramidal neurons. Unlike traditional learning rules, BTSP learns pre-post correlations on timescales of seconds and rapidly changes single-unit activity in only a few trials. To study how BTSP-like learning can be integrated into network models, we propose a generalized theoretical framework, gBTSP, which we apply to unsupervised and supervised tasks in feedforward and recurrent networks. We show that unsupervised gBTSP learns place field maps in the feedforward case and attractor memories in the recurrent case. For supervised learning, we derive how plateau events can reduce task error, enabling gBTSP to solve trajectory matching and delayed non-match-to-sample tasks. Finally, we find that the speed of credit assignment via gBTSP is limited by network depth or CA3-like recurrence, suggesting that additional mechanisms are necessary to account for BTSP-driven few-shot learning in naturalistic settings.

title: Preemptive solving of future problems: Multitask Preplay in humans and machines
summary_zh: 本文提出了一种名为多任务预演的算法，通过在任务间迁移经验来预测未追求任务的解决方案。在深度强化学习中，该算法比传统规划方法更准确地预测了人类对新任务的泛化。
summary_en: This paper proposes an algorithm called Multitask Preplay, which leverages experience from one task to predict solutions for other tasks. In deep reinforcement learning, it predicts human generalization to novel tasks more accurately than traditional planning methods.
insights: 创新点：提出多任务预演算法
方法亮点：通过经验迁移预测未追求任务的解决方案
关键发现：在深度强化学习中预测泛化能力优于传统方法
insights_en: Novelty: Introduction of the Multitask Preplay algorithm
Method highlight: Predicting solutions for unpursued tasks through experience transfer
Key finding: Superior prediction of generalization in deep reinforcement learning compared to traditional methods
abstract: Humans can pursue a near-infinite variety of tasks, but typically can only pursue a small number at the same time. We hypothesize that humans leverage experience on one task to preemptively learn solutions to other tasks that were accessible but not pursued. We formalize this idea as "Multitask Preplay", an algorithm that replays experience on one task as the starting point for "preplay"-counterfactual simulation of an accessible but unpursued task. Preplay is used to learn a predictive representation that can support fast, adaptive task performance later on. When implemented within deep reinforcement learning, it predicts human generalization to novel tasks more accurately than traditional planning and predictive representation methods across grid-worlds and a 2D Minecraft domain. Additionally, Multitask Preplay improves an artificial agent's ability to generalize to new environments sharing task co-occurrence structure. These findings demonstrate that Multitask Preplay is a scalable theory of human counterfactual learning and generalization; endowing artificial agents with this capacity can significantly improve their performance in challenging multitask environments.

Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
summary_zh: 本文研究在2+1维模拟相对论量子场。使用二维原子玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体中的自旋分量。实验表明，长波模式编码了辛-戈登模型。
summary_en: This paper studies the analog simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2+1 dimensions. It uses spin components in a two-dimensional atomic Bose-Einstein condensate. Experiments show that the long-wavelength modes encode the sine-Gordon model.
insights: 创新点：首次在二维系统中模拟相对论量子场
方法亮点：利用原子玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体实现模拟
关键发现：长波模式编码辛-戈登模型
insights_en: Novelty: First analog simulation of relativistic quantum fields in a two-dimensional system
Method highlight: Utilizing a two-dimensional atomic Bose-Einstein condensate for the simulation
Key finding: Long-wavelength modes encode the sine-Gordon model
abstract: Abstract Quantum field theories provide fundamental models of complex interacting systems 1–3 , from high-energy physics and cosmology to condensed matter. However, solving these models in non-perturbative and dynamical regimes is often challenging, particularly in more than one spatial dimension. Analogue simulation using tunable synthetic quantum systems can both verify existing theoretical predictions and lead to physical insights. Here we realize analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time), using two coherently coupled spin components 4,5 in a uniform two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate 6,7 . Specifically, we encode the paradigmatic sine-Gordon model 8,9 in the long-wavelength modes of the field describing the relative phase, ϕ , of the two components. In the perturbative regime, collective field excitations exhibit a relativistic dispersion with a tunable mass gap. We also observe explicitly non-perturbative phenomena, including the existence of topological domain walls across which ϕ rapidly winds by 2π (ref. 10 ). Our work opens possibilities for studies of cosmologically relevant phenomena including preheating 11,12 , dynamics of topological defects 13,14 and relativistic false-vacuum decay 15–19 .

title: When No-Reference Image Quality Models Meet MAP Estimation in Diffusion Latents
summary_zh: 研究无参考图像质量模型在扩散潜在空间中的应用。
summary_en: This study investigates the application of no-reference image quality models in the diffusion latent space.
insights: 创新点：首次将NR-IQA模型应用于图像增强
方法亮点：在扩散潜在空间中进行梯度优化
关键发现：不同NR-IQA模型产生不同的增强输出
insights_en: Novelty: First application of NR-IQA models in image enhancement
Method highlight: Gradient optimization in the diffusion latent space
Key finding: Different NR-IQA models yield different enhancement outputs
abstract: Contemporary no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) models can effectively quantify perceived image quality, often correlating strongly with human perceptual scores on standard IQA benchmarks. Yet few studies have explored their use as natural image priors for real-world image enhancement and compared them from a perceptual optimization perspective. In this work, we show, for the first time, that NR-IQA models can be plugged into the maximum a posteriori (MAP) framework for image enhancement. Specifically, we perform gradient-based optimization in the diffusion latent space rather than the raw pixel domain, leveraging a pretrained differentiable and bijective diffusion process. Different NR-IQA models yield different enhancement outputs, which facilitate model comparison from a new computational perspective. Guided by rankings obtained under the proposed framework, we develop an improved NR-IQA model by incorporating design elements from other highly ranked methods. Its enhancement outputs are preferred over those of its predecessors while maintaining high image fidelity.

title: Optimal scenario design for climate emulation
summary_zh: 本研究提出了一种优化气候仿真的场景设计方法，通过引入可微分的简单气候模型，提高了仿真的泛化能力。
summary_en: This study introduces an optimal scenario design method for climate emulation, enhancing the generalization ability of the emulator by incorporating a differentiable simple climate model.
insights: 创新点：提出了一种优化气候仿真的场景设计方法
方法亮点：引入可微分的简单气候模型
关键发现：提高了仿真的泛化能力
insights_en: Novelty: Proposed an optimal scenario design method for climate emulation
Method highlight: Introduced a differentiable simple climate model
Key finding: Enhanced the generalization ability of the emulator
abstract: As deep learning for physical systems continues to grow in popularity, efforts to improve generalizability have primarily focused on designing architectures that embed physical constraints. However, for machine-learning surrogate climate models (emulators), we show that the low structural diversity in existing scenarios commonly used to generate training data places a ceiling on predictive skill. Here, we examine whether training datasets themselves can be optimized to improve generalization. We introduce a method to create datasets that produce emulators capable of generalizing to new, structurally different scenarios absent from the training data. We use a differentiable simple climate model (SCM) to calculate the sensitivity of emulator loss to perturbations in the training data, iteratively updating the training data to maximize emulator skill. For an SCM, an emulator trained on one scenario optimized in this fashion outperforms an emulator trained on six standard Scenario Model Intercomparison Project (ScenarioMIP) pathways. We achieve this higher predictive skill despite training on a smaller dataset, finding that our emulator successfully isolates distinct physical behaviors of different climate forcing agents (e.g., greenhouse gases vs. aerosols) without single-forcing runs. We then demonstrate that scenarios optimized using an SCM, when used to drive an intermediate-complexity climate model, produce a training dataset that yields a more skillful emulator than training on ScenarioMIP outputs. Our results suggest that, in the compute-constrained environment of running full-scale climate models, generating a small number of dynamically rich scenarios provides greater marginal value for emulation and characterizing system responses than expanding the suite of traditional emissions pathways.

title: Decoherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect
summary_zh: 研究非厄米皮肤效应的相干性。实验采用光子量子行走。结果表明非厄米皮肤效应在去相位下可维持。
summary_en: Investigates the coherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect. Experiments use photonic quantum walks. Results indicate the skin effect persists under dephasing.
insights: 创新点：非厄米皮肤效应在去相位下的相干性研究
方法亮点：利用光子量子行走实验
关键发现：非厄米皮肤效应在去相位下可维持
insights_en: Novelty: Coherence resilience of non-Hermitian skin effect under dephasing
Method highlight: Utilizing photonic quantum walk experiments
Key finding: Skin effect persists under dephasing
abstract: Decoherence and dissipation, arising from interactions with the environment, can exert a dual influence on transport in physical systems, suppressing coherent propagation while inducing diffusion and mitigating localization in disordered systems. Non-Hermitian physics offers a distinct scenario, where structured dissipation induces directional bulk-to-boundary transport, known as the non-Hermitian skin effect. Whether such transport can persist, be enhanced, or hindered under decoherence remains a largely open question. Here we experimentally address this question using photonic quantum walks with two tunable prototypical decoherence channels, dephasing and amplitude damping. Under dephasing, the non-Hermitian skin effect survives up to the fully incoherent regime and is observed to even be enhanced by dephasing, yielding drift velocities that exceed those of coherent dynamics. By contrast, amplitude damping shows a pronounced order dependence: applied before the non-Hermitian loss operator, it suppresses and ultimately eliminates the non-Hermitian skin effect in the fully incoherent limit; applied afterward, the non-Hermitian skin effect persists and can be enhanced at sufficiently large loss strengths. Our work bridges quantum and classical non-Hermitian dynamics, demonstrates the resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect to decoherence, and opens avenues for harnessing decoherence to enhance directional transport in noisy, nonequilibrium systems. Decoherence, often viewed as detrimental to coherent transport, can instead enhance the non-Hermitian skin effect, which persists into the fully incoherent regime. Its effect can be tuned by the type and implementation of decoherence.

SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
_topics: spatial intelligence in visual foundation models
summary_zh: 针对视觉基础模型的空间推理能力不足，提出SpaRRTa基准，评估识别静态方向关系的能力。与3D目标不同，SpaRRTa关注方向关系识别。
summary_en: Addressing the limited spatial reasoning capabilities of visual foundation models, introduces SpaRRTa benchmark to evaluate the ability to identify static directional relations between visible objects. Unlike 3D objectives, SpaRRTa focuses on directional relation recognition.
insights: 创新点：提出SpaRRTa基准评估空间推理能力
方法亮点：SpaRRTa关注方向关系识别而非精确度量预测
关键发现：SpaRRTa评估模型的空间意识而非特定3D目标
insights_en: Novelty: Introduces SpaRRTa benchmark for evaluating spatial reasoning
Method highlight: SpaRRTa focuses on directional relation recognition rather than precise metric prediction
Key finding: SpaRRTa evaluates the spatial awareness of models rather than specific 3D objectives
abstract: Abstract Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible objects. Unlike traditional 3D objectives that focus on precise metric prediction (e.g., surface normal estimation), SpaRRTa probes a fundamental capability underpinning more advanced forms of human-like spatial understanding. SpaRRTa generates an arbitrary number of photorealistic images with diverse scenes and fully controllable object arrangements, along with freely accessible spatial annotations. Evaluating a range of state-of-the-art VFMs, we reveal significant disparities in their ability to encode directional spatial relations. Through our analysis, we provide insights into the mechanisms that support or hinder this form of spatial awareness in modern VFMs. We hope that SpaRRTa will serve as a useful tool for guiding the development of future spatially aware visual models. Our project page can be found at https://sparrta.gmum.net/ .

title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
summary_zh: 事件视界望远镜合作通过毫米波干涉测量合成地球大小的孔径，首次重建M87*黑洞阴影图像。图像呈现为环状结构，代表M87*周围的引力透镜和红移发射。
summary_en: The Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*.
insights: 创新点：独立干涉测量确认M87*黑洞阴影
方法亮点：使用毫米波干涉测量合成地球大小的孔径
关键发现：M87*周围存在引力透镜和红移发射
insights_en: Novelty: Independent interferometric observation confirms the black hole shadow in M87*
Method highlight: Earth-sized aperture synthesized using millimetre radio interferometry
Key finding: Gravitational lensing and redshifted emission around M87*
abstract: Abstract A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image 1–4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features 3,5–7 , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source 8,9 . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
summary_zh: 研究记录全球岛屿蜜蜂种类，发现岛屿蜜蜂多样性丰富，物种丰富度与岛屿面积和隔离度相关。
summary_en: The study presents the first global checklist of island bees, revealing rich bee diversity and the relationship between species richness and island area and isolation.
insights: 创新点：全球岛屿蜜蜂种类记录
方法亮点：分析岛屿蜜蜂多样性
关键发现：物种丰富度与岛屿特征相关
insights_en: Novelty: Global checklist of island bees
Method highlight: Analysis of bee diversity on islands
Key finding: Species richness relates to island characteristics
abstract: Abstract Islands harbor a disproportionate share of global biodiversity 1 , yet insects, even invaluable pollinators such as bees 2 , remain underrepresented in island biogeography research 3 . Here, we present the first global checklist of island bees, recording 4,140 species across 306 islands. Although islands comprise only ∼5% of Earth’s land area, they support ∼20% of global bee diversity, and 43% of insular species are endemic, making up ∼8% of all known bee species. Island bee species richness, mirroring continental trends 4 , peaks at mid-latitudes. Native richness increases with island area and declines with isolation, consistent with patterns in other taxa 5 . The strength of species–area relationships varies among biomes and is steepest in mediterranean-type systems, which also support disproportionately high bee richness relative to flowering plant diversity. Endemism is highest on large tropical islands, reflecting extensive in situ diversification. Major centers of bee endemism include Madagascar, Malesia (e.g. the Greater Sundas and New Guinea), and Hawai’i, where a single large radiation of Hylaeus ( Nesoprosopis ) dominates 6 . Among islands capable of supporting endemic species, endemism scales strongly with total richness. These findings highlight the need to integrate island bee diversity into global conservation planning and position bees as a model for understanding insect evolution and conservation on islands.

Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
summary_zh: 研究探讨了修改牛顿动力学（MOND）在解释星系团平衡中的作用。
summary_en: This study explores the role of Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters.
insights: 创新点：提出MOND可能解释星系团的暗物质问题
方法亮点：结合MOND和星系团观测数据进行分析
关键发现：MOND可能减少星系团的暗物质需求
insights_en: Novelty: Suggested that MOND may explain the dark matter problem in galaxy clusters
Method highlight: Analyzed data combining MOND and galaxy cluster observations
Key finding: MOND may reduce the dark matter requirement in galaxy clusters
abstract: First proposed by Milgrom in 1983 as an alternative to the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) paradigm, Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) has gained renewed momentum in light of persistent nondetections of exotic dark matter particles and growing tensions facing CDM on galactic scales. While MOND perfectly reproduces galactic rotation curves, it encounters notable challenges in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters. Although it reduces the overall dark matter budget in these massive systems, an unidentified mass component remains required. This paper investigates the hypothesis that this missing mass is baryonic: composed of nonradiating ordinary matter such as stellar remnants, gas too diffuse to initiate star formation, or compact, ultra-dense clouds of cold molecular gas with low volume filling factors. Using a sample of 106 clusters mapped in X-rays, emitted by the hot intracluster medium composing most of the visible mass, we derive first the total mass within the Newtonian dynamics, assuming hydrostatic equilibrium and spherical symmetry. Then, with the modified Poisson equation, we reconstruct the spatial distribution of the invisible missing matter within the MOND framework. In the sample, the relaxed systems harboring cooling flows, known as cool-core clusters, have the highest peaks of dark missing mass. Its density profile reveals a pronounced central concentration bounded by a steep truncation immediately beyond a core radius of 20 to 30 kpc, confirming previous studies. MOND reduces the necessary dynamical mass by a factor of 4 to 10. The residual missing mass is proportional to the total gas mass, being roughly twice lower.

title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
summary_zh: 研究证明了一次性系统识别的零一法则。随机输入样本可唯一确定系数。
summary_en: The study proves a zero-one law for one-shot system identification. Random input samples can uniquely determine the coefficients.
insights: 创新点：一次性系统识别的零一法则
方法亮点：分析系统识别理论
关键发现：随机输入样本的唯一性
insights_en: Novelty: Zero-one law for one-shot system identification
Method highlight: Analytic system identification theory
Key finding: Uniqueness of random input samples
abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

insights_en: Novelty: Proposal of ecological foundation models
Method highlight: Training on large, multi-modal ecological datasets
Key finding: Challenge for machine learning
abstract: Ecology aims to explain and predict how organisms interact with each other and their environments across space and time. Yet both ecological data and theory are fragmented, leading to models that generalize poorly beyond specific systems or scales. Empirical evidence spans diverse modalities, resolutions and contexts, while theory is distributed across partially overlapping frameworks that are rarely integrated within a single predictive model. We argue that ecological foundation models (ecoFMs), trained on large, multi-modal ecological datasets and informed by ecological theory, offer a route towards unifying data and theory within a common framework. Beyond their scientific value for ecology, ecoFMs present a challenging and consequential testbed for machine learning, demanding advances in multi-modal representation learning, theory-guided modelling and uncertainty-aware inference. By learning shared representations of organisms, environments and interactions, ecoFMs could improve generalization, link pattern to process and enable synthesis across ecological subdisciplines. We outline a roadmap for developing ecoFMs, including requirements for data infrastructure, model architectures, evaluation strategies and governance, and assess where current machine learning and ecological approaches fall short. If developed responsibly and collaboratively with ecological practitioners and other actors, ecoFMs could enable new modes of analysis and strengthen ecological forecasting, while simultaneously driving advances in machine learning for multi-modal integration, theory-guided learning and generalization in complex, data-limited systems. Ecology struggles to make broad predictions, as ecological data and theories are scattered across many different sources, scales and approaches. Gardiner et al. propose to create ecological foundation models, which combine large, multi-modal ecological datasets with ecological theory, as a way to create more generalizable and predictive models.

title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
summary_zh: 研究使用无缺陷费米气体在可编程传输几何中研究超流体的耗散。发现几何效应对超流体耗散有显著影响。
summary_en: This study uses a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to study superfluid dissipation. It finds that geometric effects significantly influence superfluid dissipation.
insights: 创新点：研究低维超流体的量子电阻悖论
方法亮点：使用无缺陷费米气体
关键发现：几何效应显著影响耗散
insights_en: Novelty: Studying the quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
Method highlight: Using a defect-free unitary Fermi gas
Key finding: Geometric effects significantly influence dissipation
abstract: Abstract Resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section. Yet, in low-dimensional superconductors and superfluids, residual resistance arises from topological fluctuations of the order parameter, manifesting as phase slips in one-dimensional (1D) and vortices in two-dimensional (2D) systems. How resistance and dissipation evolve as geometry interpolates between these regimes remains an open question. This evolution is masked in solid-state experiments by disorder, impurities and geometric imperfections 1–3 , and poses theoretical challenges due to competing dissipative processes and pronounced finite-size effects. Here, we use a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox: in the crossover from one dimension to two dimensions, the resistance reaches a minimum. There, widening a channel increases its resistance. Narrower, quasi-1D channels show dissipation described by Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber–Halperin theory of phase slips 4 . In this regime, varying the channel width yields the predicted exponential scaling of the activation factor over many orders of magnitude. Wider, quasi-2D channels show dissipation consistent with phase-slip events described by a finite-size vortex model 5 . The minimal dissipation in the dimensional crossover reflects a transition in the dominant dissipative mechanism, with both 1D and 2D events simultaneously suppressed. Our measurements suggest a route to minimizing dissipation in superconducting devices and provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts aimed at describing the dimensional crossover.
